record.paper_title: On free curves and related open problems
record.context_brief: Terao conjecture for free line arrangements
record.original_question: Let A be a line arrangement in the complex projective plane P^2, defined by a reduced homogeneous polynomial f, and call A free when its module D0(f) of Jacobian syzygies is a free rank-2 module over C[x,y,z]. If another line arrangement B has an intersection lattice isomorphic to that of A, must B also be free?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1. Terao’s Conjecture holds for any free line arrangement A.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2 = \mathbb{P}^2_{\mathbb{C}}$ with homogeneous coordinate ring $S = \mathbb{C}[x,y,z]$. A line arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ in $\mathbb{P}^2$ is the zero locus of a reduced homogeneous polynomial $f \in S$ that factors as a product of distinct linear forms. Define the module of Jacobian syzygies (also called the module of logarithmic derivations vanishing on $f$) by
$$ D_0(f) = \{(a,b,c) \in S^3 : a f_x + b f_y + c f_z = 0\}, $$
where $f_x, f_y, f_z$ are the partial derivatives of $f$. The arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ is called free if $D_0(f)$ is a free $S$-module (necessarily of rank $2$).

The intersection lattice $L(\mathcal{A})$ of $\mathcal{A}$ is the poset, ordered by reverse inclusion, consisting of $\mathbb{P}^2$ together with all the lines of $\mathcal{A}$ and all intersection points of pairs of distinct lines of $\mathcal{A}$.

Question: Suppose $\mathcal{A}$ is a free line arrangement in $\mathbb{P}^2$ and $\mathcal{B}$ is another line arrangement in $\mathbb{P}^2$ whose intersection lattice $L(\mathcal{B})$ is isomorphic, as a poset, to $L(\mathcal{A})$. Must $\mathcal{B}$ also be free?
artifact.category_tag: Terao's freeness conjecture for line arrangements
artifact.status_search_result: Terao's conjecture—that freeness of a hyperplane arrangement depends only on its intersection lattice—remains a famous open problem, including in the line-arrangement case in $\mathbb{P}^2$. Partial results verify the conjecture for line arrangements of small size (e.g., up to 13 lines) and for special classes such as inductively free arrangements, but no proof or counterexample for line arrangements in general is known.

status_evidence.title: Freeness and near freeness are combinatorial for line arrangements in small degrees
status_evidence.snippet: Terao conjecture saying that the freeness is determined by the combinatorics has been proven for arrangements of 13 lines in the complex projective plane.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture verified only in small cases, indicating it is still open in general.

status_evidence.title: Investigating Terao's Freeness Conjecture With Computer Algebra (MPI MIS)
status_evidence.snippet: Terao's main open conjecture in this area was formulated about 40 years ago and asks whether the freeness of the derivation module is determined by the underlying matroid.
status_evidence.claim: Terao's conjecture is explicitly described as an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: On free curves and related open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture: Terao's Conjecture holds for any free line arrangement A.
status_evidence.claim: Stated as a conjecture (open) for line arrangements.
